title: Line up a motor's belt pulley with a blower's pulley 290 mm away
instruction: Line up the motor's pulley with the blower's pulley. Slide and turn the loose motor on its base plate, keeping it on the plate and the same distance from the blower, until its pulley's outer face is in the same plane as the blower pulley's outer face, so the straightedge laid across both faces touches each pulley at both rims. Then let go of the motor and the straightedge and move both grippers away.
context: Belt-drive air handlers and exhaust fans have a motor on an adjustable base driving the fan through V-belts. After a motor is replaced or its base is moved, its pulley (sheave) is lined up with the fan's before the belts go on: a straightedge laid across both pulleys' outer faces should touch each pulley at both rims. Gates' guidance limits a V-belt drive's total misalignment, angular plus parallel, to 1/2 degree; more wears belts fast. Here the pulleys are 290 mm apart, so 1/2 degree is 2.53 mm of offset, or 0.56 mm of turn across the motor's 64 mm pulley: the hard part is sliding and turning a loose motor on its plate into that band without lifting it. The score is the alignment itself; a straightedge, the trade's tool for reading it, is supplied. Routine maintenance for HVAC mechanics and installers (O*NET 49-9021.00, about 0.4 million US workers) and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00, about 1.5 million).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five things are on the table. (1) Blower, fixed, dark grey painted steel: a housing box 120 mm along x, 100 mm along y and 140 mm tall standing on the table at x 27.0 to 39.0 cm, y -20.0 to -10.0 cm; from its front face (toward the arms) a 16 mm grey steel shaft runs 20 mm along -x, its axis 52 mm above the table at y -15.0 cm, carrying a black cast-iron pulley 90 mm across and 20 mm thick (x 23.0 to 25.0 cm, its bottom 7 mm above the table). The pulley's outer face, toward the arms, is the line x 23.0 cm. (2) Motor base plate, fixed: light grey galvanised steel, 160 mm along x, 130 mm along y, 12 mm thick, on the table at x 26.2 to 42.2 cm, y 7.5 to 20.5 cm. (3) Motor, loose, 150 g in all (a blue 3D-printed shell, a grey steel shaft, a black printed pulley): a body box 90 mm long, 70 mm wide and 80 mm tall; from the middle of one end face a 16 mm shaft 25 mm long, then a pulley 64 mm across and 18 mm thick. Its centre of mass is 40 mm above the body's underside, 9 mm from the body's centre toward the pulley. The shaft's axis is 40 mm above the body's underside (52 mm above the table: level with the blower's); the pulley's outer face is 88 mm from the body's centre and its bottom 8 mm above the body's underside. The motor stands on the plate, the centre of the body's underside at x 33.0 cm, y 14.0 cm, its shaft pointing toward the arms, turned 3 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from square: the centre of its pulley's outer face is at x 24.21 cm, 12.1 mm behind the line. (4) Straightedge, loose: a bare silver aluminium box section 20 x 40 mm with 1.2 mm walls, 480 mm long, 180 g, standing on a 20 mm face (40 mm tall) on the felt, its length along y, its centre at x 15.0 cm, y -4.5 cm (it spans y -28.5 to +19.5 cm). (5) Felt strip, fixed: green felt 40 mm along x, 500 mm along y, 2 mm thick, under the straightedge, centred at x 15.0 cm, y -4.5 cm. The pulleys' centres are 290 mm apart (y -15.0 and +14.0 cm). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: F is the centre of the motor pulley's outer face; e is how far F is behind (+) or in front of (-) the line x 23.0 cm, the blower pulley's outer face; theta is the motor's turn about the vertical from square, signed and never folded (turned round is 180 degrees out); alpha = atan(|e| / 290 mm). Total misalignment M = |theta| + alpha, in degrees: angular plus parallel, added as the belt maker adds them. Checked on every control step of the trial: (f) on its plate: the lowest bottom corner of the motor's body within 2 mm of the plate's top, the centre of its underside over the plate and its up axis within 10 degrees of vertical (so lifting it more than 2 mm off the plate, even for one step, breaks it; rocking onto an edge that stays on the plate does not); (g) on its line: the centre of the body's underside within 10 mm of y 14.0 cm (the 290 mm centre distance). One step that breaks (f) or (g), or on which the motor's pose cannot be read, scores 0 for the whole trial. Checked at the end: (a) at rest: over the last 0.5 s F moved less than 2 mm in all and the motor turned less than 0.5 degree in all; (b) upright within 2 degrees; (c) flat on its plate: all four bottom corners of the body inside the plate's outline and within 2 mm of its top; (d) on its line, as (g); (e) hands off on every step of the last 0.5 s: both grippers read and each one's tool centre point and pad-tip point at least 60 mm from the motor's and the straightedge's bounding boxes (a fully open finger reaches 57 mm out, so open fingers resting on either fail). A step on which a gripper cannot be read is not hands off. With (a) to (g) all met: 1.0 if M <= 0.5 degree (the V-belt limit: an offset alone up to 2.53 mm, or a turn alone up to 0.5 degree, 0.56 mm across the 64 mm pulley); 0.5 if M <= 1.0 degree (5.06 mm alone); 0.25 if M <= 2.0 degrees (10.1 mm alone); else 0. At the start M is 5.39 degrees (e +12.1 mm, theta 3 degrees): 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0; every trial has exactly one. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s. Holding the motor or the straightedge fails (e); lifting or carrying the motor, at any time, fails (f); sliding it along y fails (g); turning it round fails through theta; pushing it past the line costs through e. In a real trial: with the straightedge flat on the blower pulley's face, feeler gauges read the gaps g1 and g2 at the motor pulley's two rims (64 mm apart): e = (g1 + g2)/2, theta = asin(|g1 - g2| / 64 mm). With the motor proud, a try-square against each rim and a steel rule read d1 and d2 from a tape line at x 20.0 cm: e = (d1 + d2)/2 - 30 mm, theta = asin(|d1 - d2| / 64 mm). A side video, level with the plate's top, with a card ruled 2 mm above that top behind the motor, reads (f) on every frame; a tape mark at y 14.0 cm with ticks 10 mm either side reads (g); the same video shows both grippers clear at the end.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic (chosen, above printed plastic on steel). Simplified: the shafts are level by construction, so only the motor's slide and turn are scored; equal groove-to-face thicknesses, so face alignment is groove alignment. The motor is a 150 g printed shell so one gripper holds it; a production motor of this shaft size is several kilograms and takes more push. Not modelled: the belt, base bolts.
reset_notes: Put the motor back on its plate: the centre of its body's underside at x 33.0 cm, y 14.0 cm, turned 3 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from square, its pulley face 12.1 mm behind the line. Stand the straightedge back on its 20 mm face on the felt, along y, centred at x 15.0 cm, y -4.5 cm. The blower, the plate and the felt are fixed; nothing is consumed.
